title: Sur la distribution des nombres premiers
inputAbstract: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis on the complex zeros of zeta(s), we investigate the remainder term pi(x) - Li(x) in the distribution of prime numbers and establish the asymptotic bound pi(x) = Li(x) + O(sqrt(x) log x), improving the classical zero-free region estimate.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (a); Acta Math. 24 (1901), 159-182
goldVerbatimQuote: The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to pi(x) = Li(x) + O(sqrt(x) log x).

title: Sharper bounds for the Chebyshev functions theta(x) and psi(x). II
inputAbstract: In this paper, bounds given in the first part of the paper are strengthened. In addition, assuming the Riemann hypothesis, explicit inequalities are given for |psi(x) - x|, |theta(x) - x|, and |pi(x) - Li(x)| < sqrt(x) log(x) / (8 pi) for all x >= 2657, improving unconditional estimates.
goldAuthority: Math. Comp. 30 (1976), Corollary 1, p. 339
goldVerbatimQuote: If the Riemann hypothesis is true, then |pi(x) - Li(x)| < sqrt(x) log(x) / (8 pi) for all x >= 2657.

title: Grandes valeurs de la fonction somme des diviseurs et hypothese de Riemann
inputAbstract: We study the maximal order of the sum-of-divisors function sigma(n) and prove that the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if sigma(n) < e^gamma n log log n for every integer n > 5040.
goldAuthority: Sutherland https://math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/ (ArithChallenge.lean `robin_inequality`); J. Algebra 86 (1984)
goldVerbatimQuote: RH is true if and only if sigma(n) < e^gamma n log log n for every integer n > 5040.

title: An Elementary Problem Equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis
inputAbstract: This paper shows the equivalence of the Riemann hypothesis to an sequence of elementary inequalities involving the harmonic numbers H_n, the sum of the reciprocals of the integers from 1 to n. Specifically, sum_{d|n} d <= H_n + exp(H_n) log(H_n) for all n >= 1 holds if and only if the Riemann hypothesis holds.
goldAuthority: Sutherland https://math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/ (ArithChallenge.lean `lagarias_inequality`); Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002)
goldVerbatimQuote: Theorem 1.1: Problem E [sigma(n) <= H_n + exp(H_n) log(H_n) for all n >= 1] is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis.

title: On the least prime in an arithmetical progression
inputAbstract: Assuming the Extended Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-series mod k, we prove that for coprime integers k and l, the least prime p congruent to l modulo k satisfies p = O(k^{2 + epsilon}), sharpening O(k^c) bounds.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (i); J. Indian Math. Soc. 1 (1934)
goldVerbatimQuote: Chowla showed GRH for Dirichlet L-functions implies the first prime p = a mod m is O(m^2 (log m)^2).

title: The Least Quadratic Non Residue
inputAbstract: Assuming the Extended Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions L(s, chi), we show that the least positive quadratic non-residue modulo an odd prime p is O((log p)^2), improving unconditional character-sum bounds.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (f); Ann. of Math. 55 (1952), 65-72
goldVerbatimQuote: GRH for all Dirichlet L-functions implies that the first nonmember of every proper subgroup of (Z/mZ)* is O((log m)^2).

title: Riemann's hypothesis and tests for primality
inputAbstract: We present two algorithms for testing primality of an integer n. The first algorithm is shown to run in deterministic polynomial time O((log n)^4 log log log n) assuming the Extended Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, while randomized primality testing and later unconditional algorithms run without it.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (f); Sutherland scope note; J. Comput. System Sci. 13 (1976)
goldVerbatimQuote: Gary Miller introduced a deterministic primality test that he could prove runs in polynomial time using GRH for all Dirichlet L-functions.

title: Explicit bounds for primality testing and related problems
inputAbstract: Many number-theoretic algorithms rely on a result of Ankeny, which states that if the Extended Riemann Hypothesis (ERH) is true, any nontrivial subgroup G of (Z/mZ)* omits a positive integer less than c(log m)^2. Here we show that for Dirichlet characters modulo m, one may take c = 2, giving a deterministic primality witness bound 2(log n)^2.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (f); Math. Comp. 55 (1990), Theorem 2
goldVerbatimQuote: Bach showed GRH for all Dirichlet L-functions implies each proper subgroup of (Z/mZ)* is missing some integer from 1 to 2(log m)^2.

title: Complete Vinogradov 3-primes theorem under the Riemann hypothesis
authors: J.-M. Deshouillers, G. Effinger, H. te Riele, D. Zinoviev
inputAbstract: We outline a proof that if the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis holds for Dirichlet L-functions, then every odd number above 5 is a sum of three prime numbers, closing the finite gap below Vinogradov's unconditional asymptotic threshold.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (g); Electron. Res. Announc. Amer. Math. Soc. 3 (1997)
goldVerbatimQuote: Deshouillers, Effinger, te Riele, and Zinoviev showed GRH for all Dirichlet L-functions implies the odd Goldbach conjecture for all odd n >= 7.

title: Conditional bounds for the least quadratic non-residue and related problems
authors: Youness Lamzouri, Xiannan Li, Kannan Soundararajan
inputAbstract: This paper studies explicit and theoretical bounds for several interesting quantities in number theory, conditionally on the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. Specifically, we improve the existing explicit bounds for the least quadratic non-residue and the least prime in an arithmetic progression.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 items (f, k); arXiv:1309.3595 Section 1 (Dirichlet L-functions L(s, chi))
goldVerbatimQuote: Assume GRH for Dirichlet L-functions L(s, chi) modulo q; then the least prime p = a (mod q) satisfies p <= (phi(q) log q)^2.

title: Prime Twins and Siegel Zeros
inputAbstract: We investigate the distribution of prime twins under the hypothesis that exceptional real Landau-Siegel zeros of real primitive Dirichlet L-functions L(s, chi) exist infinitely often, violating the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and deduce that infinitely many twin primes p, p+2 would exist.
goldAuthority: Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 47 (1983), 193-224, Theorem 1
goldVerbatimQuote: If real primitive Dirichlet characters possess exceptional Siegel zeros infinitely often (violating Dirichlet GRH), then there are infinitely many twin primes.

title: On Artin's conjecture
inputAbstract: Artin conjectured that any integer a not equal to -1 or a perfect square is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes p with positive asymptotic density. Assuming the extended Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions of Kummer fields Q(zeta_q, a^{1/q}), we prove Artin's conjecture.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (h); Sutherland scope statement; Crelle 225 (1967)
goldVerbatimQuote: Hooley showed GRH for Dedekind zeta-functions of all number fields Q(a^{1/n}, zeta_n) implies Artin's primitive root conjecture.

title: On Euclidean rings of algebraic integers
inputAbstract: Let K be an algebraic number field whose ring of integers O_K has infinitely many units. Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions of Kummer extensions of K, we prove that O_K is a principal ideal domain if and only if it is Euclidean.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (j); Proc. Symp. Pure Math. 24 (1973), 321-332
goldVerbatimQuote: Weinberger showed that GRH for Dedekind zeta-functions implies every ring of algebraic integers with an infinite unit group is Euclidean if it has class number 1.

title: Effective versions of the Chebotarev density theorem
authors: Jeffrey C. Lagarias, Andrew M. Odlyzko
inputAbstract: We prove effective unconditional and conditional versions of the Chebotarev density theorem for finite Galois extensions L/K of algebraic number fields. Under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta function zeta_L(s), the remainder term is O(x^{1/2} log(d_L x^{[L:Q]})).
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (d); Sutherland scope statement; Algebraic Number Fields (1977), 409-464
goldVerbatimQuote: Sharp estimates in the Chebotarev density theorem follow from GRH for Dedekind zeta-functions.

title: Lower bounds for discriminants of number fields
inputAbstract: Unconditional lower bounds for root discriminants |D|^{1/n} of algebraic number fields of degree n are derived from Stark's zeta-function identities, and sharper asymptotic constants are established assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (o); Tohoku Math. J. 27 (1975), 361-382
goldVerbatimQuote: Odlyzko showed GRH for Dedekind zeta-functions implies sharper lower bounds on |disc(K)|^{1/n}.

title: Ramanujan's ternary quadratic form
inputAbstract: In 1916 Ramanujan observed that only finitely many positive odd integers fail to be represented by x^2 + y^2 + 10z^2; unconditional results show finitely many exceptions exist. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for quadratic Dirichlet L-functions and quadratic twists of an elliptic-curve L-function, we prove the 18 known odd integers are the only exceptions.
goldAuthority: MathOverflow Q17209 item (l); Invent. Math. 130 (1997), 415-454
goldVerbatimQuote: Ono and Soundararajan showed GRH for Dirichlet L-functions of quadratic characters and for quadratic twists of the L-function of an elliptic curve over Q implies the 18 known exceptions are the only ones.

title: Chebyshev's Bias
inputAbstract: The title refers to the fact, noted by Chebyshev in 1853, that primes congruent to 3 modulo 4 seem to predominate over those congruent to 1. Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and the Grand Simplicity Hypothesis (linear independence over Q of positive imaginary parts of zeros of Dirichlet L-functions), we prove the logarithmic density exists and compute it.
goldAuthority: Exp. Math. 3 (1994), 173-197, Section 1 (requires both GRH and GSH linear independence)
goldVerbatimQuote: Assuming GRH and GSH (linear independence of positive ordinates of nontrivial zeros), the logarithmic density delta(q; a, b) exists.

title: Knottedness is in NP, modulo GRH
inputAbstract: Given a tame knot K presented in the form of a knot diagram, we show that the problem of determining whether K is knotted is in the complexity class NP, assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH). In other words, unknottedness is in coNP, complementing Hass, Lagarias, and Pippenger's result that unknottedness is in NP.
goldAuthority: arXiv:1112.0845 main.tex Section 3 (invokes Koiran -> Lagarias-Odlyzko & Weinberger Dedekind Chebotarev; Lackenby 2016 proved NP unconditionally)
goldVerbatimQuote: Koiran's theorem relies on the effective Chebotarev density theorem of Lagarias, Montgomery, and Odlyzko and Weinberger, which assumes GRH [for Dedekind zeta functions].

title: On the complexity of torus knot recognition
inputAbstract: We show that the problem of recognizing that a knot diagram represents a specific torus knot, or any torus knot at all, is in the complexity class NP intersect co-NP, assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis.
goldAuthority: arXiv:1706.04424 torusknots.tex Section 5 (explicitly cites Lagarias-Odlyzko & Weinberger effective Chebotarev)
goldVerbatimQuote: The generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) is used via the effective Chebotarev density theorem [Lagarias-Odlyzko, Weinberger].

title: The supersingular isogeny path and endomorphism ring problems are equivalent
inputAbstract: We prove that the path-finding problem in ell-isogeny graphs and the endomorphism ring problem for supersingular elliptic curves are equivalent under reductions of polynomial expected time, assuming the generalised Riemann hypothesis. Previously, only heuristic reductions were known.
goldAuthority: arXiv:2111.01481 paper.tex Section 3 (Theorem thm:primebinaryform cites [LO77] Lagarias-Odlyzko effective Chebotarev)
goldVerbatimQuote: Theorem 3.2 (assuming GRH, [LO77]): primes represented by a binary quadratic form of discriminant D via Lagarias-Odlyzko effective Chebotarev.

title: Do All Elliptic Curves of the Same Order Have the Same Difficulty of Discrete Log? (Expander graphs based on GRH)
authors: David Jao, Stephen D. Miller, Ramarathnam Venkatesan
inputAbstract: The aim of this paper is to justify the common cryptographic practice of selecting elliptic curves using their order as the primary criterion. Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), we prove that the isogeny graph of ordinary elliptic curves with the same endomorphism ring is an expander graph, yielding a random self-reducibility reduction for ECDLP.
goldAuthority: arXiv:math/0411378 jmv-arxiv-sep-02-2005.tex Section 3.1 (\label{heckelfunc}: Hecke character and modular eigenform L-functions)
goldVerbatimQuote: Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for L(s, chi) [where chi is a nontrivial Hecke character of the imaginary quadratic class group and weight-2 eigenform L-functions].

title: Constructing elliptic curve isogenies in quantum subexponential time
authors: Andrew M. Childs, David Jao, Vladimir Soukharev
inputAbstract: Given two elliptic curves over a finite field having the same cardinality and endomorphism ring, it is known that the curves admit an isogeny between them, but finding such an isogeny is believed to be computationally difficult. Here we give a subexponential-time quantum algorithm for constructing isogenies, assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (but with no other assumptions).
goldAuthority: arXiv:1012.4019 main.tex Section 2 (invokes Jao-Miller-Venkatesan Hecke character GRH and Bach Dedekind ERH class-group generators)
goldVerbatimQuote: Assuming GRH, by Jao, Miller, and Venkatesan [Hecke L-functions] and Bach [ERH for Dedekind zeta functions generating Cl(O_K)].

title: New large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials
inputAbstract: We prove new unconditional upper bounds for the frequency with which Dirichlet polynomials can take large values. As a consequence, we show unconditionally that N(sigma, T) <= T^{(30/13)(1 - sigma) + o(1)}, improving Ingham's zero-density bound toward the Density Hypothesis and yielding primes in intervals [x, x + x^{17/30 + o(1)}].
goldAuthority: arXiv:2405.20552 Section 1 (unconditional zero-density theorem)
goldVerbatimQuote: We prove unconditionally N(sigma, T) <= T^{(30/13)(1 - sigma) + o(1)}.

title: Linear equations in primes
inputAbstract: Consider a system Psi of non-constant affine-linear forms psi_1,...,psi_t: Z^d -> Z, no two of which are linearly dependent. Let N be a large integer. We give an asymptotic formula for the number of prime tuples (psi_1(n),...,psi_t(n)) with n in [-N,N]^d, conditional on the Mobius and Nilsequences conjecture MN(s-1) and the Gowers Inverse conjecture GI(s) (both subsequently proved unconditionally; no Riemann Hypothesis is assumed).
goldAuthority: arXiv:math/0606088 Section 1 (mentions GRH only in historical comparison with Balog/Hardy-Littlewood; main theorem unconditional on RH/GRH)
goldVerbatimQuote: Main theorem assumes MN(s-1) and GI(s) (later proved unconditionally by Green-Tao-Ziegler 2012), never RH or GRH.
